title: Certificates of Deposit: Deciding Whether a Maturity Payout Account Has Been Closed
content:
Among the bank's Certificates of Deposit, a certificate whose Maturity Instruction pays the balance out relies on the account that receives it. This page fixes when such a Maturity Instruction can be carried out as written, and how the bank decides that its receiving account has been closed.

## Paying out only into an open account

Money sent out under a Maturity Instruction can go only to an account that has not been closed. With the payout account still open, nothing stands in the way: at the end of grace the whole balance leaves as a maturity payout into that account, and the certificate is closed. A Maturity Instruction to mail a check pays the entire balance by official check.

## The closure test

The test applies to a Maturity Instruction of one of two kinds: paying out to a checking account, or paying out to a savings account. For such a Maturity Instruction:

- the account examined is the one recorded on the certificate as its payout account;
- it is examined in the product family the Maturity Instruction pays to, that is the savings account records for a payout to savings and the checking account records for a payout to checking;
- the account's status decides: a status of closed means the payout account has been closed. Any other status means it has not.

A Maturity Instruction to renew, and one to mail a check, name no receiving account in this sense, and the closure test does not touch them.

## Input, judgement, outcome (hypothetical records)

| Maturity Instruction on the certificate | Status of the recorded payout account | Payout account closed? |
|---|---|---|
| Pay out to savings | Savings account: closed | Yes |
| Pay out to savings | Savings account: active | No; the payout runs as written when grace ends |
| Pay out to checking | Checking account: closed | Yes |
| Pay out to checking | Checking account: dormant | No; only a closed status counts |
| Renew | (any) | Not tested |
| Mail a check | (any) | Not tested |
